title: FICO cuts workforce by 15% as part of AI-driven restructuring
key_facts: Fair Isaac (FICO) said it will cut about 15% of its workforce as part of a broader restructuring and AI integration.
It did not specify the number; with 3,811 employees at end September 2025, about 570 workers could be affected.
It began notifying employees this week.
About $27 million in pre-tax charges expected in Q4 fiscal 2026, mainly severance; plan largely complete by Q3 fiscal 2027.
Shares are down about 58% this year as US regulators seek to loosen its hold on mortgage credit scoring.
Last month the FHFA directed Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to allow all lenders to use VantageScore.
quote_evidence: Credit-scoring giant Fair Isaac, known as FICO, said on Tuesday it would trim about 15 per cent of its workforce as part of a broader restructuring and AI integration, becoming the latest US company to cut jobs as businesses automate tasks and redirect spending toward the technology.
It did not specify the number of employees laid off.
why_it_matters_hint: 15% cut tied to AI restructuring while shares fall on mortgage scoring changes.
